94	  vim.b[bufnr].quick_edit = on
95	  vim.diagnostic.enable(not on, { bufnr = bufnr })
96	end

100	  callback = function(args)

102	      apply_quick_edit(args.buf, true)
103	    end
104	  end,

111	  if arg == "on" then
112	    target = true
113	  elseif arg == "off" then
114	    target = false
115	  else
116	    target = not vim.b[bufnr].quick_edit
117	  end
118	  apply_quick_edit(bufnr, target)

120	end, {
121	  nargs = "?",

3	-- Two pieces:

5	--      so `fd` discovers all repos under <group>/<repo> (e.g. JingleAI/X,

10	--   2. persistence.nvim — per-cwd session save/restore. Snacks's projects
11	--      picker default `confirm = "load_session"` calls `:lua
12	--      require("persistence").load()` after `:tcd`, which restores buffers,
13	--      windows, tabs, and even nvim-tree state from the last time you were
14	--      in that repo. Without persistence, `load_session` is a no-op and you
15	--      just get a `:tcd` + file picker.
16	--
17	-- Why /Volumes/Data/Program (not ~/Documents/Program):
18	--   ~/Documents/Program is a symlink to /Volumes/Data/Program. fd's
19	--   --absolute-path resolves through the symlink, so listing the canonical
20	--   side avoids duplicate entries in the picker.
21	--
22	-- Three pickers compared (all useful, different scope):
23	--   * `<leader>fp` (this) → snacks projects: oldfiles + dev fd, with session
24	--                           restore on confirm.

26	--                           plain :tcd, no session restore.
27	--   * `prefix+g` (tmux)   → sesh: spawn/switch tmux session per project,
28	--                           launches nvim+lazygit in fresh windows.
29	-- See docs/tools/sesh.md for the comparison table.

37	    opts = {
38	      -- One session file per cwd, stored under stdpath("state")/sessions/
39	      options = { "buffers", "curdir", "tabpages", "winsize", "help", "globals", "skiprtp" },
40	      -- Don't auto-save sessions for ephemeral try-cli projects (they
41	      -- accumulate noise) or for the home dir (no project context).
42	      need = 1, -- save session when at least 1 buffer is open

44	    keys = {

46	      { "<leader>ql", function() require("persistence").load({ last = true }) end, desc = "Restore last session" },
47	      { "<leader>qd", function() require("persistence").stop() end,             desc = "Don't save current session" },

10	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
11	-- Quick-edit mode: when nvim is invoked as $EDITOR by another tool (OpenCode
12	-- ctrl+x+e, Claude Code ctrl+g, `crontab -e`, `git commit`, etc.), the buffer
13	-- is a throwaway scratch file under a tempdir. We don't want markdownlint
14	-- diagnostics or format-on-save mangling the agent's prompt or the cron line
15	-- the user is typing.
16	--
17	-- Detection (heuristic, two-track):
18	--
19	--   1. Path-based: buffer's full path lives under a known tempdir prefix
20	--      ($TMPDIR, /tmp, /var/folders, /private/var/folders) OR matches a
21	--      known scratch-file pattern (crontab.*, COMMIT_EDITMSG, *.tmp.*).
22	--   2. Env-based explicit override: NVIM_QUICK_EDIT=1 forces ON,
23	--      NVIM_QUICK_EDIT=0 forces OFF (escape hatches for either direction).
24	--
25	-- When quick-edit is detected we:
26	--   - set `vim.b.autoformat = false` (LazyVim's per-buffer format-on-save toggle)
27	--   - disable diagnostics for that buffer (kills MD034 et al.)
28	--   - leave LSP, treesitter, syntax highlight, keymaps untouched -- still
29	--     a usable editor, just no autofix / red squigglies.
30	--
31	-- Toggle manually with `:QuickEditMode` if you need to flip it mid-session.
32	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	
34	local function tempdir_prefixes()
35	  local prefixes = { "/tmp/", "/var/folders/", "/private/var/folders/", "/private/tmp/" }
36	  local tmpdir = vim.env.TMPDIR
37	  if tmpdir and tmpdir ~= "" then
38	    -- normalise: ensure trailing slash, resolve symlinks
39	    local resolved = vim.uv.fs_realpath(tmpdir) or tmpdir
40	    if not resolved:match("/$") then
41	      resolved = resolved .. "/"
42	    end
43	    table.insert(prefixes, resolved)
44	  end
45	  return prefixes
46	end
47	
48	local function is_quick_edit_path(path)
49	  if not path or path == "" then
50	    return false
51	  end
52	  local resolved = vim.uv.fs_realpath(path) or path
53	
54	  -- Path under a known tempdir
55	  for _, prefix in ipairs(tempdir_prefixes()) do
56	    if resolved:sub(1, #prefix) == prefix then
57	      return true
58	    end
59	  end
60	
61	  -- Known scratch-file basenames regardless of location
62	  local base = vim.fn.fnamemodify(resolved, ":t")
63	  local patterns = {
64	    "^crontab%.", -- crontab -e -> /tmp/crontab.XXXXXX/crontab on some systems
65	    "^COMMIT_EDITMSG$", -- git commit (.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG)
66	    "^MERGE_MSG$",
67	    "^TAG_EDITMSG$",
68	    "^EDIT_DESCRIPTION$", -- gh / glab PR description editor
69	    "%.tmp%.", -- generic *.tmp.* (OpenCode, Claude Code)
70	  }
71	  for _, pat in ipairs(patterns) do
72	    if base:match(pat) then
73	      return true
74	    end
75	  end
76	  return false
77	end
78	
79	local function detect_quick_edit(bufnr)
80	  -- Explicit env override wins
81	  local env = vim.env.NVIM_QUICK_EDIT
82	  if env == "1" or env == "true" then
83	    return true
84	  end
85	  if env == "0" or env == "false" then
86	    return false
87	  end
88	  local name = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(bufnr)
89	  return is_quick_edit_path(name)
90	end
91	
92	local function apply_quick_edit(bufnr, on)
93	  vim.b[bufnr].autoformat = not on -- LazyVim format-on-save per-buffer toggle
94	  vim.b[bufnr].quick_edit = on
95	  vim.diagnostic.enable(not on, { bufnr = bufnr })
96	end
97	
98	vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd({ "BufReadPost", "BufNewFile" }, {
99	  group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("user_quick_edit", { clear = true }),
100	  callback = function(args)
101	    if detect_quick_edit(args.buf) then
102	      apply_quick_edit(args.buf, true)
103	    end
104	  end,
105	})
106	
107	vim.api.nvim_create_user_command("QuickEditMode", function(opts)
108	  local arg = (opts.args or ""):lower()
109	  local bufnr = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
110	  local target
111	  if arg == "on" then
112	    target = true
113	  elseif arg == "off" then
114	    target = false
115	  else
116	    target = not vim.b[bufnr].quick_edit
117	  end
118	  apply_quick_edit(bufnr, target)
119	  vim.notify("QuickEditMode: " .. (target and "ON (no lint, no format-on-save)" or "OFF"))
120	end, {
121	  nargs = "?",
122	  complete = function()
123	    return { "on", "off" }
124	  end,

126	})

```text
1	-- Zoxide picker for jumping between projects without leaving Neovim.
2	--
3	-- Why this exists:
4	--   * Day-to-day cd between repos lives in tmux/sesh land, but when you're
5	--     deep in a 5-window nvim session and need to peek at another repo's file
6	--     ("how did I solve X over there?"), spawning a new tmux session adds
7	--     ceremony. <leader>fz lets you jump cwd-as-vim-cwd in-place.
8	--
9	-- Two modes:
10	--   <leader>fz   — pick a zoxide entry, change buffer-local cwd via :tcd
11	--                  (only this tab follows; other tabs keep their cwd)
12	--   <leader>fZ   — pick a zoxide entry, change global cwd via :cd
13	--                  (whole nvim session moves; matches LazyVim file-pickers'
14	--                   default scope)
15	--
16	-- Why :tcd as the default:
17	--   LazyVim auto-detects project root per buffer; switching global cwd can
18	--   make file-pickers do confusing things if you have buffers from multiple
19	--   projects open. :tcd keeps the change scoped to the current tab.
20	--
21	-- Falls back gracefully if `zoxide` binary isn't on PATH (no error, key just
22	-- does nothing — guard inside the function).
23	
24	local function zoxide_pick(scope)
25	  if vim.fn.executable("zoxide") == 0 then
26	    vim.notify("zoxide not installed", vim.log.levels.WARN)
27	    return
28	  end
29	
30	  -- Get scored list from zoxide. Format: "<score> <path>" per line.
31	  local out = vim.fn.systemlist({ "zoxide", "query", "--list", "--score" })
32	  if vim.v.shell_error ~= 0 or #out == 0 then
33	    vim.notify("zoxide DB is empty", vim.log.levels.INFO)
34	    return
35	  end
36	
37	  -- Parse into snacks.picker items. Score is shown as a comment column.
38	  local items = {}
39	  for _, line in ipairs(out) do
40	    local score, path = line:match("^%s*([%d%.]+)%s+(.+)$")
41	    if score and path and vim.fn.isdirectory(path) == 1 then
42	      table.insert(items, {
43	        text = path,
44	        score_text = score,
45	        file = path,
46	        dir = path,
47	      })
48	    end
49	  end
50	
51	  if #items == 0 then
52	    vim.notify("zoxide returned no valid directories", vim.log.levels.WARN)
53	    return
54	  end
55	
56	  Snacks.picker({
57	    title = "Zoxide" .. (scope == "global" and " (cd)" or " (tcd)"),
58	    items = items,
59	    format = function(item)
60	      -- Two-column layout: score (right-aligned 8 chars) + path
61	      local short = item.text:gsub("^" .. vim.pesc(vim.env.HOME), "~")
62	      return {
63	        { ("%8s "):format(item.score_text), "Number" },
64	        { short, "Directory" },
65	      }
66	    end,
67	    preview = "directory",
68	    confirm = function(picker, item)
69	      picker:close()

 `./pitfalls/nvim-fs-find-enoent-stale-cwd.md`

```text
1	# nvim 0.12 startup ENOENT from vim.fs.find via avante / lualine / lazy checker
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	
5	- `vim.schedule callback: vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory`
6	- `[C]: in function 'assert'` followed by `vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'`
7	- Source frames: `lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:106` (avante)
8	- Source frames: `lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:55` (lualine)
9	- Often paired with: `lualine: Failed to refresh statusline: ... vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT`
10	- Triggered from: `lazy/manage/checker.lua` (background plugin update check) or
11	  `lualine.refresh` immediately after startup
12	- One-shot at startup; nvim continues to function but the popup is noisy
13	
14	**First seen**: 2026-04 (Neovim 0.12.1, macOS, Apple Silicon)
15	**Affects**: Neovim **0.12.x** + LazyVim + avante.nvim + lualine.nvim. Did not
16	occur on 0.11.x.
17	**Status**: workaround = `cd` to a real directory before launching nvim. No
18	upstream issue filed (regression in `runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua`).
19	
20	## Symptom
21	
22	Verbatim from a real session:
23	
24	```
25	Error  20:05:51 msg_show.lua_error vim.schedule callback: vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory
26	stack traceback:
27		[C]: in function 'assert'
28		vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'
29		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:106: in function <...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:102>
30		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:167: in function 'detect'
31		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:206: in function 'get_project_root'
32		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/suggestion.lua:43: in function 'new'
33		...4/.local/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/init.lua:425: in function '_init'
34		...
35		...al/share/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/manage/checker.lua:43: in function 'fast_check'
36	
37	Error  20:06:04 msg_show.lua_error vim.schedule callback: ...share/nvim/lazy/lualine.nvim/lua/lualine/utils/utils.lua:211: lualine: Failed to refresh statusline:
38	...ee84/.local/share/nvim/lazy/lualine.nvim/lua/lualine.lua:433: Lua: vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory
39	stack traceback:
40		[C]: in function 'assert'
41		vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'
42		....local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:55: in function <....local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:52>
43		....local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:106: in function 'detect'
44		...
45	```
46	
47	Both stacks bottom out at the **same** `[C]: in function 'assert'` →
48	`vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'` frame.
49	
50	## Root cause
51	
52	In Neovim **0.12**, `runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua` added an unguarded `assert` on
53	the result of `vim.uv.cwd()` inside the upward-walking branch of
54	`vim.fs.find()`:
55	
56	```lua
57	-- runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua, around line 716
58	local cwd = assert((iswin and prefix:match('^%w:$')) and uv.fs_realpath(prefix) or uv.cwd())
59	```
60	
61	`uv.cwd()` returns `nil, "ENOENT", "ENOENT: no such file or directory"`
62	when the process's current working directory has been **deleted out from
63	under the running shell** — the classic cases:
64	
65	- `git switch` / `git checkout` to a branch where the current directory
66	  doesn't exist
67	- `rm -rf` the directory you're sitting in (often via `yazi`, `oil`,
68	  `lazygit`, or another tmux pane)
69	- `mv` the parent directory away
70	- The shell that launched nvim was started in a directory that has since
71	  been deleted
72	
73	When `uv.cwd()` returns nil, the `assert()` raises, which surfaces as the
74	generic `vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory` traceback —
75	**with no hint that the real culprit is a missing cwd**.
76	
77	Two innocent callers happen to trigger this at startup:
78	
79	1. **`avante.nvim`** (`utils/root.lua:106`) calls `vim.fs.find(..., { path =
80	   M.bufpath(buf) or vim.uv.cwd(), upward = true })` from
81	   `suggestion.lua:43` during `_init()`. If `bufpath` is nil for the
82	   current buffer (no name yet, scratch, dashboard), the fallback hits the
83	   stale cwd.
84	2. **`LazyVim`** (`util/root.lua:55`) does the same pattern, called from
85	   `util/lualine.lua` on every `lualine.refresh()` — so the error fires
86	   continuously, not just once.
87	
88	The `lazy.nvim` checker frame (`lazy/manage/checker.lua:43 → git.lua:192
89	get_tag_refs`) is unrelated; it just happens to call `vim.fs.find` from a
90	scheduled callback at the same moment.
91	
92	This is **not** a bug in avante, LazyVim, lualine, or lazy — they all worked
93	on 0.11. It's a Neovim 0.12 regression: the new assert in `vim.fs.find`
94	turns a previously-recoverable nil-cwd into a hard error.
95	
96	## Workaround
97	
98	**Immediate (per-session):** cd to a directory that exists and re-launch
99	nvim:
100	
101	```sh
102	cd ~ && nvim
103	# or, from inside the broken nvim:
104	:cd ~
105	:e
106	```
107	
108	To verify which side is wrong (your shell vs nvim itself):
109	
110	```sh
111	pwd                    # if this errors, your shell's cwd is gone
112	ls "$(pwd)"            # confirm the dir actually exists on disk
113	nvim --headless -c 'lua print(vim.uv.cwd())' -c 'qa!'
114	# nil = stale cwd, the assert will fire
115	```
116	
117	**Defensive (per-machine, optional):** add a pre-startup guard to your
118	shell rc — if `pwd` fails, jump to `$HOME` before launching interactive
119	tools. Not added to this repo's `dot_config/zsh/` because the failure mode
120	is loud enough to notice and the underlying state (`rm -rf $PWD`) usually
121	indicates the user already knows.
122	
123	**Code-level workaround (not applied):** monkey-patch `vim.fs.find` to fall
124	back to `vim.fn.expand("~")` when `uv.cwd()` is nil, e.g. in
125	`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. Skipped because (a) upstream will
126	likely revert/guard the assert, (b) silently rewriting cwd hides genuine
127	state corruption, (c) the trigger is rare in practice.
128	
129	## Prevention
130	
131	- Don't `rm -rf` or `git switch`-away from the directory a long-lived
132	  shell is sitting in. If you must, `cd ~` first.
133	- Tools that delete-then-recreate the cwd (some `git worktree` workflows,
134	  container rebuilds, `mise` cache resets) are the most common root cause —
135	  prefer `cd` out before the destructive action.
136	- If you see the symptom *without* having deleted the cwd, the next
137	  suspect is your shell's `chpwd`/`precmd` racing with a background
138	  process; check `~/.config/zsh/` hooks.
139	
140	Not graduated to a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant: trigger is user-action-driven,
141	not a config-level trap that recurs across machines.
142	
143	## Related
144	
145	- Upstream source: `runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua` line ~716 in Neovim 0.12.x
146	  (`assert((iswin and prefix:match('^%w:$')) and uv.fs_realpath(prefix) or uv.cwd())`)
147	- Affected callers in this repo's plugin set:
148	  - `lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:106` (`detectors.pattern`)
149	  - `lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:55` (also `detectors.pattern`)
150	- No upstream issue filed at neovim/neovim, avante.nvim, or LazyVim as of
151	  2026-04. If this recurs across multiple users, file at
152	  https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues with the verbatim traceback and
153	  the `nvim --headless -c 'lua print(vim.uv.cwd())'` repro.
154
```

# Findings: Cursor-style file-reference feature — existing utilities to reuse

Config layout is minimal: only two lua dirs exist — `lua/config/` and `lua/exact_plugins/` (verified via `find`). There is **no `lua/util/` or helper module** — I'll flag that under Q3.

## 1. Clipboard config — CONFIRMED, fully wired

**File: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`** (the whole file, 20 lines)

```lua
6   vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
...
12  if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
13    local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
14    vim.g.clipboard = {
15      name = "OSC 52",
16      copy = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"), ["*"] = osc52.copy("*") },
17      paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
18    }
19  end
```

- Line 6: `clipboard = "unnamedplus"` — so **`"+` IS the system clipboard**, and unnamed yanks also route there.
- Lines 12-18: over SSH, `+`/`*` are re-routed through OSC 52 (`require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")`). Locally, LazyVim's default provider (pbcopy) is used.
- **Implication for your feature:** `vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)` (or `vim.fn.setreg("+", ref, "c")`) is the correct, SSH-safe way to copy — it lands in the local terminal clipboard both locally and remotely. Do **not** shell out to `pbcopy` yourself; that breaks the OSC 52 path.
- CLAUDE.md corroboration: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/CLAUDE.md:206` documents this OSC 52 pairing with tmux `set-clipboard on`.

## 2. Project / git root detection — use `LazyVim.root`

There is no hand-rolled rooter, but LazyVim's root util is loaded globally and already used in this repo.

**In-repo usage:** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/nvim/lua/exact_plugins/floating-tui.lua:10` → `cwd = LazyVim.root.git()`.

# Neovim Keybinding Structure — Findings

This is a **LazyVim**-based config. Note: `lua/exact_plugins/` is chezmoi's directory — the `exact_` prefix is a chezmoi attribute, so the live target is `~/.config/nvim/lua/plugins/`. The `.lua` files inside are plain Lua (not templated), as you said.

## Leader key
`<leader>` = **Space**. It is *not* set in this repo (grep for `mapleader` in the repo returns nothing). It's inherited from LazyVim's default at `/Users/david/.local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/config/options.lua:2`:
```lua
vim.g.mapleader = " "
```
(`<localleader>` = `\` there too.) So `<leader>a` = **space then a**.

## Top-level structure of the nvim config
```
dot_config/nvim/
  init.lua                      -> require("config.lazy")
  lua/config/
    lazy.lua                    -> bootstraps lazy.nvim; spec = { LazyVim import "lazyvim.plugins", { import = "plugins" } }
    options.lua                 -> clipboard/OSC52 (no keymaps except opts)
    keymaps.lua                 -> custom keymaps + one which-key group
    autocmds.lua                -> quick-edit-mode autocmd (no keymaps)
  lua/exact_plugins/            -> (live: lua/plugins/) per-plugin lazy specs
    avante.lua, copilot.lua     -> AI plugins
    floating-tui.lua            -> Snacks terminal keys + which-key group
    flash.lua, mini-surround.lua, vim-visual-multi.lua, gitsigns.lua,
    diffview.lua, colorscheme.lua, dashboard.lua, projects.lua,
    zoxide-picker.lua, vim-tmux-navigator.lua, nvim-cmp.lua,
    noice-fix.lua, wakatime.lua, example.lua
```
Enabled LazyVim extras (`dot_config/nvim/lazyvim.json`) — these pull in keymaps defined *outside* the repo:
```
lazyvim.plugins.extras.ai.claudecode      <- defines the <leader>a "+ai" group
lazyvim.plugins.extras.ai.copilot
lazyvim.plugins.extras.coding.mini-surround, coding.nvim-cmp, ...
```

- Lines 12-19: over SSH, route `+`/`*` registers through OSC 52.

Relevant collisions to avoid for a new yank map:

 `./pitfalls/nvim-fs-find-enoent-stale-cwd.md`

```text
1	# nvim 0.12 startup ENOENT from vim.fs.find via avante / lualine / lazy checker
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	
5	- `vim.schedule callback: vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory`
6	- `[C]: in function 'assert'` followed by `vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'`
7	- Source frames: `lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:106` (avante)
8	- Source frames: `lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:55` (lualine)
9	- Often paired with: `lualine: Failed to refresh statusline: ... vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT`
10	- Triggered from: `lazy/manage/checker.lua` (background plugin update check) or
11	  `lualine.refresh` immediately after startup
12	- One-shot at startup; nvim continues to function but the popup is noisy
13	
14	**First seen**: 2026-04 (Neovim 0.12.1, macOS, Apple Silicon)
15	**Affects**: Neovim **0.12.x** + LazyVim + avante.nvim + lualine.nvim. Did not
16	occur on 0.11.x.
17	**Status**: workaround = `cd` to a real directory before launching nvim. No
18	upstream issue filed (regression in `runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua`).
19	
20	## Symptom
21	
22	Verbatim from a real session:
23	
24	```
25	Error  20:05:51 msg_show.lua_error vim.schedule callback: vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory
26	stack traceback:
27		[C]: in function 'assert'
28		vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'
29		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:106: in function <...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:102>
30		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:167: in function 'detect'
31		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:206: in function 'get_project_root'
32		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/suggestion.lua:43: in function 'new'
33		...4/.local/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/init.lua:425: in function '_init'
34		...
35		...al/share/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/manage/checker.lua:43: in function 'fast_check'
36	
37	Error  20:06:04 msg_show.lua_error vim.schedule callback: ...share/nvim/lazy/lualine.nvim/lua/lualine/utils/utils.lua:211: lualine: Failed to refresh statusline:
38	...ee84/.local/share/nvim/lazy/lualine.nvim/lua/lualine.lua:433: Lua: vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory
39	stack traceback:
40		[C]: in function 'assert'
41		vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'
42		....local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:55: in function <....local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:52>
43		....local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:106: in function 'detect'
44		...
45	```
46	
47	Both stacks bottom out at the **same** `[C]: in function 'assert'` →
48	`vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'` frame.
49	
50	## Root cause
51	
52	In Neovim **0.12**, `runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua` added an unguarded `assert` on
53	the result of `vim.uv.cwd()` inside the upward-walking branch of
54	`vim.fs.find()`:
55	
56	```lua
57	-- runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua, around line 716
58	local cwd = assert((iswin and prefix:match('^%w:$')) and uv.fs_realpath(prefix) or uv.cwd())
59	```
60	
61	`uv.cwd()` returns `nil, "ENOENT", "ENOENT: no such file or directory"`
62	when the process's current working directory has been **deleted out from
63	under the running shell** — the classic cases:
64	
65	- `git switch` / `git checkout` to a branch where the current directory
66	  doesn't exist
67	- `rm -rf` the directory you're sitting in (often via `yazi`, `oil`,
68	  `lazygit`, or another tmux pane)
69	- `mv` the parent directory away
70	- The shell that launched nvim was started in a directory that has since
71	  been deleted
72	
73	When `uv.cwd()` returns nil, the `assert()` raises, which surfaces as the
74	generic `vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory` traceback —
75	**with no hint that the real culprit is a missing cwd**.
76	
77	Two innocent callers happen to trigger this at startup:
78	
79	1. **`avante.nvim`** (`utils/root.lua:106`) calls `vim.fs.find(..., { path =
80	   M.bufpath(buf) or vim.uv.cwd(), upward = true })` from
81	   `suggestion.lua:43` during `_init()`. If `bufpath` is nil for the
82	   current buffer (no name yet, scratch, dashboard), the fallback hits the
83	   stale cwd.
84	2. **`LazyVim`** (`util/root.lua:55`) does the same pattern, called from
85	   `util/lualine.lua` on every `lualine.refresh()` — so the error fires
86	   continuously, not just once.
87	
88	The `lazy.nvim` checker frame (`lazy/manage/checker.lua:43 → git.lua:192
89	get_tag_refs`) is unrelated; it just happens to call `vim.fs.find` from a
90	scheduled callback at the same moment.
91	
92	This is **not** a bug in avante, LazyVim, lualine, or lazy — they all worked
93	on 0.11. It's a Neovim 0.12 regression: the new assert in `vim.fs.find`
94	turns a previously-recoverable nil-cwd into a hard error.
95	
96	## Workaround
97	
98	**Immediate (per-session):** cd to a directory that exists and re-launch
99	nvim:
100	
101	```sh
102	cd ~ && nvim
103	# or, from inside the broken nvim:
104	:cd ~
105	:e
106	```
107	
108	To verify which side is wrong (your shell vs nvim itself):
109	
110	```sh
111	pwd                    # if this errors, your shell's cwd is gone
112	ls "$(pwd)"            # confirm the dir actually exists on disk
113	nvim --headless -c 'lua print(vim.uv.cwd())' -c 'qa!'
114	# nil = stale cwd, the assert will fire
115	```
116	
117	**Defensive (per-machine, optional):** add a pre-startup guard to your
118	shell rc — if `pwd` fails, jump to `$HOME` before launching interactive
119	tools. Not added to this repo's `dot_config/zsh/` because the failure mode
120	is loud enough to notice and the underlying state (`rm -rf $PWD`) usually
121	indicates the user already knows.
122	
123	**Code-level workaround (not applied):** monkey-patch `vim.fs.find` to fall
124	back to `vim.fn.expand("~")` when `uv.cwd()` is nil, e.g. in
125	`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. Skipped because (a) upstream will
126	likely revert/guard the assert, (b) silently rewriting cwd hides genuine
127	state corruption, (c) the trigger is rare in practice.
128	
129	## Prevention
130	
131	- Don't `rm -rf` or `git switch`-away from the directory a long-lived
132	  shell is sitting in. If you must, `cd ~` first.
133	- Tools that delete-then-recreate the cwd (some `git worktree` workflows,
134	  container rebuilds, `mise` cache resets) are the most common root cause —
135	  prefer `cd` out before the destructive action.
136	- If you see the symptom *without* having deleted the cwd, the next
137	  suspect is your shell's `chpwd`/`precmd` racing with a background
138	  process; check `~/.config/zsh/` hooks.
139	
140	Not graduated to a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant: trigger is user-action-driven,
141	not a config-level trap that recurs across machines.
142	
143	## Related
144	
145	- Upstream source: `runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua` line ~716 in Neovim 0.12.x
146	  (`assert((iswin and prefix:match('^%w:$')) and uv.fs_realpath(prefix) or uv.cwd())`)
147	- Affected callers in this repo's plugin set:
148	  - `lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:106` (`detectors.pattern`)
149	  - `lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:55` (also `detectors.pattern`)
150	- No upstream issue filed at neovim/neovim, avante.nvim, or LazyVim as of
151	  2026-04. If this recurs across multiple users, file at
152	  https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues with the verbatim traceback and
153	  the `nvim --headless -c 'lua print(vim.uv.cwd())'` repro.
154
```

```md
# Plan: Cursor-style file-reference copy keybindings in Neovim

## Context

When handing code to Claude Code (or Cursor), the useful thing to paste is a
reference like `@path/to/file`, `@path/to/file:12`, or `@path/to/file:12-40`
— the `@` triggers the agent's file-mention and the `:line[-line]` points it at
exact code. Today there is no way to grab that from Neovim; you retype paths and
line numbers by hand.

This adds four Neovim keybindings that build such a reference from the current
buffer + cursor line (normal mode) or visual selection (visual mode) and copy it
to the system clipboard, in both **project-relative** and **machine-absolute**
path flavors.

Decisions already made with the user:
- Bind under a **new `<leader>y` ("copy ref") group** — that prefix is currently
  unused (unlike the contested `<leader>a` AI group shared by avante + claudecode).
- Provide **4 explicit keys**: line-aware and file-only, each × relative/absolute.

## Keymap semantics (the contract)

`<leader>` = Space. All four work in normal **and** visual mode (`{ "n", "x" }`).

| Key | Path flavor | Normal mode | Visual mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<leader>yr` | relative | `@rel/path:12` (cursor line) | `@rel/path:12-40` (selection) |
| `<leader>ya` | absolute | `@/abs/path:12` | `@/abs/path:12-40` |
| `<leader>yf` | relative | `@rel/path` (no line) | `@rel/path` (no line) |
| `<leader>yF` | absolute | `@/abs/path` (no line) | `@/abs/path` (no line) |

Notes:
- **Line-aware keys (`yr`/`ya`) use the current cursor line in normal mode** —
  deliberately *not* whole-file — so they are meaningfully distinct from the
  file-only keys (`yf`/`yF`). This maps your three example formats to distinct
  actions: `@file` → `yf`, `@file:line` → `yr` (normal), `@file:line1-line2` →
  `yr` (visual).
- Single-line visual selection collapses `:12-12` → `:12`.
- Relative base = **git root** (`LazyVim.root.git()`); files outside the git root
  fall back to a cwd/home-relative path (`:~:.`).

## Implementation

All in one file — **`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/keymaps.lua`** (currently 14
lines; the established home for standalone maps + a `which-key.add` group, and
NOT gated by `enableVimMode` per the repo's nvim rule). No new file is added
(the sibling `lua/exact_plugins/` dir has the chezmoi `exact_` attribute, which
would delete unmanaged files — avoid touching it).

Reuse (confirmed present on this nvim 0.12.4), no new deps:
- `LazyVim.root.git()` — git root; already used at `lua/exact_plugins/floating-tui.lua:10`.
- `vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)` — builtin, returns `nil` if not a subpath.
- `vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)` — SSH-safe copy (respects the OSC52 provider set in
  `lua/config/options.lua:12-18`; do **not** shell out to `pbcopy`).
- Visual range via `vim.fn.line(".")` / `vim.fn.line("v")` — the house pattern at
  `lua/exact_plugins/gitsigns.lua:23-28`.
- `vim.notify(..., vim.log.levels.*)` — house feedback style.

Add a `copy_reference` helper + the four maps + the which-key group:

\```lua
-- Copy a Cursor-style file reference to the system clipboard, for pasting into
-- Claude Code / Cursor:  @path  |  @path:12  |  @path:12-40
-- Normal mode -> cursor line; visual mode -> selection range.
local function copy_reference(opts)
  local abspath = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(0)
  if abspath == "" then
    vim.notify("copy-ref: buffer has no file", vim.log.levels.WARN)
    return
  end
  abspath = vim.fn.fnamemodify(abspath, ":p")

  -- path component
  local path
  if opts.absolute then
    path = abspath
  else
    -- pcall guards the nvim-0.12 vim.fs.find ENOENT-on-nil-cwd trap
    -- (pitfalls/nvim-fs-find-enoent-stale-cwd.md)
    local ok, root = pcall(function() return LazyVim.root.git() end)
    path = (ok and root and vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)) or vim.fn.fnamemodify(abspath, ":~:.")
  end

  -- line component
  local mode = vim.fn.mode()
  local visual = mode == "v" or mode == "V" or mode == "\22"
  local suffix = ""
  if opts.lines then
    if visual then
      local a, b = vim.fn.line("."), vim.fn.line("v")
      if a > b then a, b = b, a end
      suffix = (a == b) and (":" .. a) or (":" .. a .. "-" .. b)
    else
      suffix = ":" .. vim.fn.line(".")
    end
  end
  if visual then
    vim.api.nvim_feedkeys(vim.keycode("<Esc>"), "n", false) -- leave visual mode
  end

  local ref = "@" .. path .. suffix
  vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)
  vim.notify("Copied " .. ref, vim.log.levels.INFO)
end

require("which-key").add({
  { "<leader>y", group = "copy ref" },
})

vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "<leader>yr", function() copy_reference({ lines = true }) end,
  { desc = "Ref: relative + line" })
vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "<leader>ya", function() copy_reference({ lines = true, absolute = true }) end,
  { desc = "Ref: absolute + line" })
vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "<leader>yf", function() copy_reference({}) end,
  { desc = "Ref: relative (file only)" })
vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "<leader>yF", function() copy_reference({ absolute = true }) end,
  { desc = "Ref: absolute (file only)" })
\```

Edge cases handled: unnamed/scratch buffer → warn + no-op; deleted cwd → `pcall`
falls back to a relative path instead of erroring; file outside git root →
`:~:.` fallback.

## Verification

1. Deploy: `chezmoi diff` then `chezmoi apply` (nvim files are copied verbatim,
   not templated) — or edit the target directly for a quick loop.
2. Headless smoke (config loads + maps registered, no Lua error):
   `nvim --headless -c 'lua print(vim.fn.maparg("<leader>yr", "n"))' -c 'qa!'`
   (expect a non-empty rhs; stderr clean).
3. Interactive, in a real project file:
   - Normal mode: `<leader>yf` → clipboard `@rel/path`; `<leader>yr` →
     `@rel/path:<curline>`. Confirm with `:echo getreg('+')` or paste.
   - Visual-select several lines → `<leader>yr` → `@rel/path:L1-L2`; single-line
     selection → `@rel/path:L`.
   - `<leader>ya` / `<leader>yF` → machine-absolute variants.
   - Press `<leader>y` → which-key shows the "copy ref" group with 4 entries.
   - No collision: `:verbose map <leader>yr` shows only our map.
   - Edge: `:enew` (unnamed) → `<leader>yf` → warning toast, no crash.
4. Real target: paste `@rel/path:12-40` into Claude Code and confirm it resolves.

## Out of scope / optional

- **Docs**: no maintenance rule mandates a doc for nvim leader-maps (the
  `Ctrl+`/`Alt+` keybinding row targets shell/tmux). Optionally, following the
  `docs/neovim/floating-tui.md` precedent, a short `docs/neovim/copy-reference.md`
  (+ `.zh-TW`, + `mkdocs.yml` nav, + `uv run mkdocs build --strict`) could be
  added later — left out to keep this change lean unless you want it.

```text
1	# Floating TUI Tools in Neovim
2	
3	Floating terminal windows for TUI tools, powered by [Snacks.terminal](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim/blob/main/docs/terminal.md) (bundled with LazyVim).
4	
5	## How It Works
6	
7	All TUI keymaps live in `lua/plugins/floating-tui.lua`. Each tool is a single `Snacks.terminal.toggle(cmd, opts)` call — no custom Lua module needed. Snacks handles:
8	
9	- Floating window lifecycle (create, show, hide, resize)
10	- Terminal session persistence (hide with `q`, reopen with same keymap)
11	- Double-Esc to exit terminal insert mode
12	- Auto-cleanup when the process exits
13	
14	This is the same mechanism behind `<leader>gg` (LazyGit via `Snacks.lazygit()`).
15	
16	## Default Keymaps
17	
18	| Keymap | Tool | Category |
19	|--------|------|----------|
20	| `<leader>gg` | LazyGit | Git (LazyVim built-in) |
21	| `<leader>zg` | gh dash | Git / GitHub |
22	| `<leader>zs` | sqlit | Database |
23	| `<leader>fy` | yazi | File Manager |
24	| `<leader>zb` | btop | System Monitor |
25	| `<leader>zd` | lazydocker | Container |
26	| `<leader>zi` | ipython | REPL |
27	
28	Inside a floating TUI window:
29	
30	- **Double-Esc** — exit terminal insert mode (back to normal mode)
31	- **q** (normal mode) — hide the window, process keeps running
32	- **Same keymap again** — reopen the hidden window
33	
34	For the managed `gh-dash` / `diffnav` / `lazygit` setup behind `<leader>zg`, see [Git Diff Workflow](../tools/git_diff_workflow.md).
35	
36	## Adding a New TUI
37	
38	Add an entry to the `keys` table in `lua/plugins/floating-tui.lua`:
39	
40	```lua
41	{
42	  "<leader>zX",
43	  function()
44	    Snacks.terminal.toggle("mytool", {
45	      win = { title = " mytool " },
46	    })
47	  end,
48	  desc = "MyTool",
49	},
50	```
51	
52	### Common Options
53	
54	```lua
55	Snacks.terminal.toggle(cmd, {
56	  cwd = vim.uv.cwd(),          -- working directory
57	  cwd = LazyVim.root.git(),    -- or use git root
58	  env = { FOO = "bar" },       -- environment variables
59	  auto_close = false,           -- keep window after process exits (for short-lived tools)
60	  win = {
61	    title = " tool name ",      -- floating window title
62	    width = 0.9,                -- 0-1 = ratio, >1 = columns
63	    height = 0.9,
64	    border = "rounded",         -- "rounded", "double", "single", "none"
65	    position = "float",         -- "float" (default for cmd), "bottom", "left", "right"
66	  },
67	})
68	```
69	
70	### Multi-word Commands
71	
72	Pass a table for commands with arguments:
73	
74	```lua
75	Snacks.terminal.toggle({ "gh", "dash" }, { ... })
76	Snacks.terminal.toggle({ "psql", "postgres://localhost/mydb" }, { ... })
77	```
78	
79	### Tools That Exit Quickly
80	
81	Some tools (like `sqlit`) may exit and show `[Process exited 0]`. Set `auto_close = false` to keep the window visible so you can inspect output. The next toggle after closing will create a fresh instance.
82	
83	### Tools with Vim-like Keybindings
84	
85	Tools that use Esc internally (like sqlit's vim mode) work fine with Snacks' **double-Esc** timer — a single Esc goes to the TUI, pressing Esc again within 200ms exits terminal insert mode.
86	
87	### Tools That Use `q` to Quit
88	
89	By default, Snacks maps `q` in normal mode to **hide** the floating window (process keeps running). However, some TUI tools (like `sqlit`) use `q` as their own quit command, which terminates the process.
90	
91	**The conflict:** if you Double-Esc back to Neovim normal mode and press `q`, Snacks hides the window — but if you press `q` while still in terminal insert mode, the TUI receives it and may exit the process entirely.
92	
93	**Solution:** Remap the Snacks hide key to `<C-q>` for these tools, so `q` is never intercepted by Snacks:
94	
95	```lua
96	Snacks.terminal.toggle("sqlit", {
97	  win = {
98	    title = " sqlit ",
99	    keys = {
100	      q = false,                              -- disable default q-to-hide
101	      hide = { "<C-q>", "hide", mode = "n" }, -- use Ctrl-q to hide instead
102	    },
103	  },
104	  auto_close = false,
105	})
106	```
107	
108	Workflow for these tools:
109	- **Double-Esc** — exit terminal insert mode
110	- **Ctrl-q** (normal mode) — hide the window, process keeps running
111	- **Same keymap** (e.g. `<leader>zs`) — reopen the hidden window
112	
113	This pattern applies to any TUI tool where `q` has special meaning (e.g. database clients, interactive viewers).
114	
115	## When to Use a Dedicated Plugin Instead
116	
117	For most TUI tools, `Snacks.terminal.toggle` is sufficient. Consider a dedicated plugin when you need:
118	
119	- **Deep Neovim integration** — e.g. `Snacks.lazygit()` auto-configures colorscheme themes and nvim-remote editing
120	- **File selection callbacks** — e.g. [yazi.nvim](https://github.com/mikavilpas/yazi.nvim) can open selected files in Neovim buffers
121	- **Output parsing / RPC** — tools that need to send structured data back to Neovim
122	
123	| Tool | Generic (Snacks) | Dedicated Plugin |
124	|------|:-:|:-:|
125	| lazygit | OK | `Snacks.lazygit()` (built-in, recommended) |
126	| yazi | OK for browsing | `yazi.nvim` if you need file-open callbacks |
127	| gh dash | OK | `gh-dash.nvim` if used daily |
128	| btop, htop, k9s, etc. | Recommended | N/A |
129
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Neovim 中的浮動 TUI 工具 (Floating TUI Tools)
2	
3	!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"
4	    技術名詞首次出現以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，例：依賴注入
5	    (dependency injection)。**不自創翻譯**——若無公認譯名直接保留英文
6	    （如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`）。代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。
7	
8	提供 TUI 工具的浮動終端視窗 (floating terminal windows)，由 [Snacks.terminal](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim/blob/main/docs/terminal.md) 驅動（隨 LazyVim 一起捆綁）。
9	
10	## 運作方式
11	
12	所有 TUI 的快捷鍵 (keymaps) 都放在 `lua/plugins/floating-tui.lua`。每個工具都是單一個 `Snacks.terminal.toggle(cmd, opts)` 呼叫——不需要自訂的 Lua 模組 (module)。Snacks 會處理：
13	
14	- 浮動視窗的生命週期 (lifecycle)（建立、顯示、隱藏、調整大小）
15	- 終端 session 持久化 (persistence)（用 `q` 隱藏、用相同快捷鍵重新開啟）
16	- 連按兩次 Esc 離開終端的 insert mode
17	- 程式結束時自動清理
18	
19	這也是 `<leader>gg`（透過 `Snacks.lazygit()` 啟動 LazyGit）背後的相同機制。
20	
21	## 預設快捷鍵
22	
23	| 快捷鍵 | 工具 | 類別 |
24	|--------|------|----------|
25	| `<leader>gg` | LazyGit | Git（LazyVim 內建） |
26	| `<leader>zg` | gh dash | Git / GitHub |
27	| `<leader>zs` | sqlit | 資料庫 |
28	| `<leader>fy` | yazi | 檔案管理員 |
29	| `<leader>zb` | btop | 系統監控 |
30	| `<leader>zd` | lazydocker | 容器 |
31	| `<leader>zi` | ipython | REPL |
32	
33	在浮動 TUI 視窗內：
34	
35	- **連按兩次 Esc** — 離開終端 insert mode（回到 normal mode）
36	- **q**（normal mode） — 隱藏視窗，程式持續執行
37	- **再次按下相同快捷鍵** — 重新開啟已隱藏的視窗
38	
39	關於 `<leader>zg` 背後託管的 `gh-dash` / `diffnav` / `lazygit` 設定，請見 [Git Diff 工作流程](../tools/git_diff_workflow.md)。
40	
41	## 新增一個 TUI
42	
43	在 `lua/plugins/floating-tui.lua` 的 `keys` 表格中加一筆：
44	
45	```lua
46	{
47	  "<leader>zX",
48	  function()
49	    Snacks.terminal.toggle("mytool", {
50	      win = { title = " mytool " },
51	    })
52	  end,
53	  desc = "MyTool",
54	},
55	```
56	
57	### 常見選項
58	
59	```lua
60	Snacks.terminal.toggle(cmd, {
61	  cwd = vim.uv.cwd(),          -- 工作目錄
62	  cwd = LazyVim.root.git(),    -- 或使用 git 根目錄
63	  env = { FOO = "bar" },       -- 環境變數
64	  auto_close = false,           -- 程式結束後保留視窗（適用於短生命週期工具）
65	  win = {
66	    title = " tool name ",      -- 浮動視窗標題
67	    width = 0.9,                -- 0-1 = 比例，>1 = 欄數
68	    height = 0.9,
69	    border = "rounded",         -- "rounded", "double", "single", "none"
70	    position = "float",         -- "float"（cmd 預設）, "bottom", "left", "right"
71	  },
72	})
73	```
74	
75	### 多字命令
76	
77	要傳入帶參數的命令時，使用 table：
78	
79	```lua
80	Snacks.terminal.toggle({ "gh", "dash" }, { ... })
81	Snacks.terminal.toggle({ "psql", "postgres://localhost/mydb" }, { ... })
82	```
83	
84	### 會快速離開的工具
85	
86	某些工具（如 `sqlit`）可能會結束並顯示 `[Process exited 0]`。設定 `auto_close = false` 可保留視窗顯示，方便檢查輸出。關閉後下次切換 (toggle) 會建立新的實例 (instance)。
87	
88	### 具有類 Vim 鍵綁定的工具
89	
90	把 Esc 用於內部按鍵的工具（例如 sqlit 的 vim mode）能與 Snacks 的 **double-Esc** 計時器良好搭配——單次 Esc 會送到 TUI，在 200ms 內再按一次 Esc 才會離開終端 insert mode。
91	
92	### 使用 `q` 退出的工具
93	
94	預設情況下，Snacks 會把 normal mode 中的 `q` 對映到**隱藏**浮動視窗（程式持續執行）。然而某些 TUI 工具（如 `sqlit`）會把 `q` 當成自己的 quit 命令，這會結束程式。
95	
96	**衝突點：** 若你按 Double-Esc 回到 Neovim 的 normal mode 並按下 `q`，Snacks 會隱藏視窗——但若你還在終端 insert mode 時按 `q`，TUI 會收到該按鍵並可能直接結束程式。
97	
98	**解法：** 把 Snacks 的隱藏鍵 (hide key) 重新對映到 `<C-q>`，這樣 `q` 永遠不會被 Snacks 攔截：
99	
100	```lua
101	Snacks.terminal.toggle("sqlit", {
102	  win = {
103	    title = " sqlit ",
104	    keys = {
105	      q = false,                              -- 停用預設的 q-to-hide
106	      hide = { "<C-q>", "hide", mode = "n" }, -- 改用 Ctrl-q 來隱藏
107	    },
108	  },
109	  auto_close = false,
110	})
111	```
112	
113	這類工具的工作流程：
114	
115	- **連按兩次 Esc** — 離開終端 insert mode
116	- **Ctrl-q**（normal mode） — 隱藏視窗，程式持續執行
117	- **相同快捷鍵**（例如 `<leader>zs`） — 重新開啟已隱藏的視窗
118	
119	這個模式適用於任何 `q` 帶有特殊意義的 TUI 工具（例如資料庫 client、互動式檢視器）。
120	
121	## 何時改用專用外掛 (Dedicated Plugin)
122	
123	對大多數 TUI 工具來說，`Snacks.terminal.toggle` 已經足夠。在以下情況才考慮專用外掛：
124	
125	- **深度 Neovim 整合** — 例如 `Snacks.lazygit()` 會自動設定 colorscheme 主題與 nvim-remote 編輯
126	- **檔案選擇 callback** — 例如 [yazi.nvim](https://github.com/mikavilpas/yazi.nvim) 可在 Neovim buffer 中開啟所選檔案
127	- **輸出解析 / RPC** — 需要把結構化資料 (structured data) 送回 Neovim 的工具
128	
129	| 工具 | 通用 (Snacks) | 專用外掛 |
130	|------|:-:|:-:|
131	| lazygit | OK | `Snacks.lazygit()`（內建，推薦） |
132	| yazi | 瀏覽用 OK | 若需要 file-open callbacks 則用 `yazi.nvim` |
133	| gh dash | OK | 若每天使用則用 `gh-dash.nvim` |
134	| btop, htop, k9s 等 | 推薦 | N/A |
135
```
</details></tool-use>

# Copy Cursor-style file references (`@file:line`)

Four Neovim keymaps that copy a **Cursor / Claude Code style file reference** —
`@path`, `@path:12`, or `@path:12-40` — to the system clipboard, built from the
current buffer plus the cursor line (normal mode) or the visual selection
(visual mode). The `@` triggers the agent's file-mention and the `:line[-line]`
points it at exact code, so you paste an exact pointer instead of retyping paths
and line numbers by hand.

All four live in `lua/config/keymaps.lua` under a `<leader>y` ("copy ref")
which-key group. Press `<leader>y` (Space then `y`) to see them.

## Keymaps

`<leader>` = Space. Every key works in **normal** and **visual** mode.

| Keymap | Path flavor | Normal mode (cursor line) | Visual mode (selection) |
|--------|-------------|---------------------------|-------------------------|
| `<leader>yr` | project-relative | `@rel/path:12` | `@rel/path:12-40` |
| `<leader>ya` | machine-absolute | `@/abs/path:12` | `@/abs/path:12-40` |
| `<leader>yf` | project-relative | `@rel/path` (no line) | `@rel/path` (no line) |
| `<leader>yF` | machine-absolute | `@/abs/path` (no line) | `@/abs/path` (no line) |

Mnemonic: `r`elative / `a`bsolute carry the line; `f`ile-only (capital `F` =
absolute) is the bare path. Together the four cover all three reference shapes:

- `@file` → `<leader>yf`
- `@file:line` → `<leader>yr` in normal mode
- `@file:line1-line2` → `<leader>yr` in visual mode

A single-line visual selection collapses `:12-12` → `:12`. After copying in
visual mode the mapping leaves visual mode and shows a `Copied @…` toast.

## Path flavors

- **Relative** (`yr` / `yf`) is resolved against the **git root**
  (`LazyVim.root.git()` — the same root used by [Floating TUI](floating-tui.md)).
  A file outside the git root falls back to a `~` / cwd-relative path.
- **Absolute** (`ya` / `yF`) is the full machine path (`expand("%:p")`), with no
  symlink resolution.

Relative is usually what you want for Claude Code (it operates inside the
project); absolute is for files outside the repo, or when a tool needs the full
path.

## Implementation notes

The feature is a ~40-line `copy_reference(opts)` helper plus four
`vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, …)` calls in `lua/config/keymaps.lua`. It reuses,
with no new dependencies:

- `LazyVim.root.git()` — git-root detection.
- `vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)` — built-in relative-path computation.
- `vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)` — respects the OSC 52 clipboard provider configured
  in `lua/config/options.lua`, so it copies into your local terminal clipboard
  even over SSH. Do **not** shell out to `pbcopy` — that bypasses OSC 52. See
  [Clipboard](../tools/clipboard.md).
- Visual range via `vim.fn.line(".")` / `vim.fn.line("v")` — the same pattern the
  gitsigns stage-selection maps use.

Edge cases: an unnamed / scratch buffer shows a `copy-ref: buffer has no file`
warning and copies nothing; a deleted cwd is guarded with `pcall` (avoids the
Neovim 0.12 `vim.fs.find` ENOENT trap) and falls back to a relative path.

## Why `<leader>y`

`<leader>y` was an unused prefix. The AI keymaps under `<leader>a` are already
crowded — avante and claudecode both bind many `<leader>a…` keys and even
collide with each other — so a fresh `y` ("yank / copy") group keeps these
reference-copy actions clear of that contention and easy to find in which-key.

To change or extend the set, edit the `copy_reference` helper and the
`vim.keymap.set` block in `lua/config/keymaps.lua`.

```

# 複製 Cursor 風格的檔案 reference (`@file:line`)

!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"
    技術名詞首次出現以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，例：依賴注入
    (dependency injection)。**不自創翻譯**——若無公認譯名直接保留英文
    （如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`）。代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。

四個 Neovim 快捷鍵 (keymaps)，把 **Cursor / Claude Code 風格的檔案 reference**
——`@path`、`@path:12` 或 `@path:12-40`——複製到系統剪貼簿 (clipboard)，內容由目前的
buffer 加上游標所在行（normal mode）或選取範圍 (visual selection)（visual mode）組成。
`@` 會觸發 agent 的檔案 mention，`:line[-line]` 則指向確切的程式碼，讓你直接貼上精準的
指標，而不用手動重打路徑與行號。

四個快捷鍵都放在 `lua/config/keymaps.lua`，歸在一個 `<leader>y`（「copy ref」）的
which-key 群組底下。按 `<leader>y`（Space 再按 `y`）即可看到它們。

## 快捷鍵

`<leader>` = Space。每個鍵在 **normal** 與 **visual** mode 都能用。

| 快捷鍵 | 路徑類型 | Normal mode（游標行） | Visual mode（選取範圍） |
|--------|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|
| `<leader>yr` | 專案相對 (project-relative) | `@rel/path:12` | `@rel/path:12-40` |
| `<leader>ya` | 機器絕對 (machine-absolute) | `@/abs/path:12` | `@/abs/path:12-40` |
| `<leader>yf` | 專案相對 | `@rel/path`（無行號） | `@rel/path`（無行號） |
| `<leader>yF` | 機器絕對 | `@/abs/path`（無行號） | `@/abs/path`（無行號） |

助記：`r`elative / `a`bsolute 會帶行號；`f`ile-only（大寫 `F` = 絕對）則是純路徑。
四個合起來涵蓋三種 reference 形態：

- `@file` → `<leader>yf`
- `@file:line` → normal mode 下的 `<leader>yr`
- `@file:line1-line2` → visual mode 下的 `<leader>yr`

單行的 visual 選取會把 `:12-12` 收斂成 `:12`。在 visual mode 複製後，該對映會離開
visual mode 並顯示 `Copied @…` 的提示 (toast)。

## 路徑類型

- **相對** (`yr` / `yf`) 以 **git 根目錄**為基準解析（`LazyVim.root.git()`，與
  [Floating TUI](floating-tui.md) 使用同一個根目錄）。git 根目錄以外的檔案會退回到
  以 `~` / cwd 為基準的相對路徑。
- **絕對** (`ya` / `yF`) 是完整的機器路徑（`expand("%:p")`），不解析 symlink。

貼給 Claude Code 時通常用相對路徑（它在專案內運作）；絕對路徑則適用於 repo 以外的
檔案，或某個工具需要完整路徑時。

## 實作細節

整個功能就是 `lua/config/keymaps.lua` 裡一個約 40 行的 `copy_reference(opts)` helper，
加上四個 `vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, …)` 呼叫。它重用了下列既有能力，不引入新的依賴
(dependency)：

- `LazyVim.root.git()` — git 根目錄偵測。
- `vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)` — 內建的相對路徑計算。
- `vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)` — 尊重 `lua/config/options.lua` 設定的 OSC 52 剪貼簿
  provider，所以即使透過 SSH 也會複製到你本機終端機的剪貼簿。**不要**直接呼叫
  `pbcopy`——那會繞過 OSC 52。詳見 [Clipboard](../tools/clipboard.md)。
- visual range 用 `vim.fn.line(".")` / `vim.fn.line("v")` 取得——與 gitsigns 的
  stage-selection 對映相同的做法。

邊界情況：未命名 / scratch buffer 會顯示 `copy-ref: buffer has no file` 警告且不複製
任何東西；被刪除的 cwd 以 `pcall` 防護（避開 Neovim 0.12 的 `vim.fs.find` ENOENT
陷阱），並退回到相對路徑。

## 為什麼選 `<leader>y`

`<leader>y` 原本是沒被用到的 prefix。`<leader>a` 底下的 AI 快捷鍵已經很擠——avante 與
claudecode 都綁了很多 `<leader>a…` 的鍵，甚至彼此互相衝突——所以另開一個 `y`
（「yank / 複製」）群組，能讓這些「複製 reference」的動作避開那塊爭用區，也更容易在
which-key 裡找到。

若要更動或擴充這組鍵，編輯 `lua/config/keymaps.lua` 裡的 `copy_reference` helper 與
`vim.keymap.set` 區塊即可。

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
